The detective training program will acquaint uniformed patrol officers with detectives’ duties by using a hands-on training approach. This training is intended to give as many officers as possible the opportunity to learn the detective function either in preparation for assignment as detectives or in helping the patrol officer be more efficient, productive, and knowledgeable.
p
A. Officers who have completed their probation shall be selected by the division commanders of the Patrol Bureau.
p
1. The officer’s placement on the eligibility list for corporal/detective rank as well as the department’s affirmative action goals shall be considered.
p
2. Officers desiring to participate may be asked to submit a letter of intent to the appropriate division commander.
p
3. Selected officers may serve in the position from twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months. Higher capacity pay shall not be authorized for this assignment.
p
B. Detective commanding officers shall develop a formal training program including a training manual to be used for officers assigned to this program.
p

C. Detectives to whom these officers are assigned remain accountable for the proper investigation of their cases. Officers shall not be assigned cases independently, but shall work with the detective.
p

The Patrol Sergeant Training Program (PSTP) is designed to facilitate the learning process for newly promoted sergeants. The purpose of the program is to ensure newly promoted sergeants are capable of adequately performing the basic job tasks and responsibilities of a sergeant assigned to the patrol function. The program will be carried out in compliance with the Patrol Sergeant Training Program Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
p

A. The Patrol Bureau Assistant Chief or their designee shall notify the Field Training Coordinator of any upcoming promotions and effective dates for Corporals/Detectives promoting to the rank of Sergeant.
p

1. All new Sergeants will be required to complete two (2) weeks of training in the field with a designated Training Sergeant prior to moving to their new assignment. During this time, the new Sergeant will be trained on all objectives identified in the Patrol Sergeant Training Program Checklist.
p

2. The Division Commander will certify the new Sergeant has completed this portion of the program. The new Sergeant will then move to their new assignment and assume supervisory responsibility for their team.
p

B. All new Sergeants will be required to complete the New Supervisor’s Course #3737 no earlier than the twelfth (12th) month before the date of promotion and no later than the first anniversary of the date of promotion to Sergeant, per TCOLE mandate and HB 3211.
p

The purpose of the New Detective Course is to ensure newly promoted corporals/detectives are capable of adequately performing the basic job tasks and responsibilities of a detective assigned to a Criminal Investigation Unit. The New Detective Course consists of forty (40) hours of instruction designed to facilitate the transition from officer to detective.
p
A. The Patrol Bureau Assistant Chief or designee shall notify the Training Division Captain of any upcoming promotions and effective dates for officers promoting to the rank of corporal/detective.
p
1. All new corporals/detectives, regardless of pending assignment, will be required to complete the forty (40) hour training program.
p
2. The Training Division staff will facilitate this training and work with approved instructors who are experienced in the investigative field.
p
3. The course training will be reported to TCOLE by the Training Division staff for continuing education hours for the newly promoted corporal/detective.
p
B. All new corporals/detectives will be required to complete the Training Division’s New Detective Course #3296, no later than the six (6) months after promoting to the rank of corporal/detective.
p
To facilitate continued leadership training at each level of command within the department; Lieutenants and Captains will be required to receive leadership training associated with their rank.
p
A. The Patrol Bureau Assistant Chief or designee shall notify the Training Division Captain of any upcoming promotions and effective dates for Lieutenants and Captains.
p
1. All new Lieutenants are required to complete a Command Level course no later than one
p
(1) year after the date of promotion.
p
2. All new Captains are required to complete an Executive Level course no later than one (1) year after the date of promotion.
p
3. Any Command Level or Executive Level courses that have been approved by the Training Division Captain that are completed prior to the date of promotion shall satisfy this requirement.
p
B. The Training Division Captain is responsible for selecting the required training courses for the Lieutenant and Captain ranks.
p
C. The Training Division Captain is responsible for the scheduling and notification of department personnel of the dates and locations of the course.
